mainTopic: The procedure for the מנחה and its leftovers, why the סוטה's מנחה is unique, and רבי שמעון's rule that a sinner's offering is kept plain.
overview: The גמרא finishes going through a ברייתא about how a מנחה is offered. It explains that the קומץ is carried up to the מזבח in a כלי שרת, salted, and burned, and then the כהנים may eat the leftovers (the שיריים). רבי חנינא and רבי יוחנן disagree about the exact moment the קומץ makes the leftovers permitted. The כהנים may eat the leftovers like kings, with wine, oil and honey, but they may not let them become חמץ. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks how it can say all מנחות need oil and frankincense when the מנחת חוטא has neither. The answer is that the סוטה's מנחה is the only one that differs in both ways: it has no oil or frankincense, and it is barley flour. רבי שמעון explains that a sinner's offering is kept plain, while offerings not brought for a sin, like the מצורע's, get נסכים. The amud ends as רבן גמליאל asks the חכמים for permission to explain the סוטה's barley offering as a symbolic lesson.

steps.title: The ברייתא: he burns the קומץ in a service vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: the כהן burns the קומץ in a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he burns it in a service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא about the מנחה procedure. This sets up a question about its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'it' is the קומץ, the handful of flour taken from the מנחה. The ברייתא seems to say the burning happens inside a כלי שרת. The next step questions exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: He burns it (on the מזבח as an offering)
A holy vessel used for the Temple service
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: And he burns it in a service vessel.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the קומץ, the handful taken from the מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the line-by-line reading of the ברייתא from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא states that the קומץ is burned 'in a כלי שרת'.

steps.title: Is it really burned inside a vessel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: the קומץ is not burned inside a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really burn it in a service vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the קומץ could be burned inside a כלי שרת. It is burned on the fire of the מזבח, not in a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about wording only. Everyone knows the burning takes place on the מזבח. So the ברייתא's phrase 'burns it in a vessel' cannot be read literally.

phrases.english: In a service vessel he burns it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's phrase 'burns it in a כלי שרת'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning happens on the fire of the מזבח, so it cannot happen inside a vessel.

steps.title: Read it as: he carries it up in a vessel to burn it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the line: the כהן brings the קומץ up to the מזבח in a כלי שרת in order to burn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: he brings it up in a service vessel in order to burn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. The vessel is used to carry the קומץ up to the מזבח, and then it is burned there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'in a כלי שרת' describes how the קומץ is carried, not where it is burned. So the ברייתא is teaching that the קומץ must be brought up in a holy vessel. The burning itself is on the fire.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings it up (to the מזבח)

phrases.english: Rather, say:
He brings it up in a service vessel in order to burn it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the burning happens inside the vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vessel is used to carry the קומץ up to the מזבח; the burning is on the fire.

steps.title: The ברייתא: he salts it and puts it on the fire
steps.stepSummary: The next line of the ברייתא says the כהן salts the קומץ and places it on the fires of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he salts it and places it on the fires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next step of the procedure: salting the קומץ and putting it on the fire. This sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds two actions. The קומץ is salted, and then it is placed on the fire of the מזבח. The next step gives the פסוק for the salting.

phrases.english: And he salts it and places it on top of the fires,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קומץ is salted and then placed on the fire of the מזבח.

steps.title: The source for salting: every מנחה gets salt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the פסוק requiring salt on every מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And every meal-offering of yours you shall season with salt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the salting with a פסוק. It says every מנחה must be salted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says plainly that every מנחה needs salt. That is why the קומץ, the part offered on the מזבח, is salted before it goes on the fire.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And every offering of your meal-offering'
you shall season with salt, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְכׇל קׇרְבַּן מִנְחָתְךָ בַּמֶּלַח תִּמְלָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the salting in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The requirement to salt the קומץ.

steps.title: The ברייתא: once the קומץ is offered, the rest is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that after the קומץ is offered, the leftover part of the מנחה is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the handful is offered, its leftovers are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: after the קומץ is offered, the כהנים may eat the rest. This sets up a question about the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering the קומץ is what permits the rest of the flour, the שיריים, to be eaten. The rule ties the eating to the offering of the קומץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Its leftovers (the rest of the מנחה)

phrases.english: Once the handful is offered, its leftovers are eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the קומץ is offered, the שיריים may be eaten.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the leftovers are eaten after the קומץ is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a standard request for a source, not an attack on the rule. The גמרא wants to see where the תורה links eating the leftovers to offering the קומץ.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that the שיריים are eaten after the קומץ is offered.

steps.title: First the memorial part is burned, then the rest goes to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two פסוקים in a row: the כהן burns the אזכרה, and what remains goes to אהרן and his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the priest shall burn its memorial part,' and it is written: 'And what is left of the meal-offering shall be for Aaron and his sons.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two פסוקים that come one after the other. First the קומץ is burned, and then the rest is given to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'memorial part' (אזכרה) is the קומץ. Right after the תורה describes burning it, it gives the leftovers to the כהנים. That order shows the eating comes after the קומץ is offered.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the priest shall burn'
its memorial part, etc.'
And it is written: 'And what is left of the meal-offering'
shall be for Aaron and his sons.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 2:2 to 2:3: burning the אזכרה is followed by the leftovers going to the כהנים, so the eating comes after the קומץ is offered.
steps.whatToRemember: Offering the קומץ is what permits the כהנים to eat the rest of the מנחה.

steps.title: 'Once the קומץ is offered' fits both opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא's phrase 'once the קומץ is offered' can be read according to either side of a known מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Once the handful is offered': each Sage can read it according to his own view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks again at the words 'once the קומץ is offered.' It says each Sage reads them his own way. This sets up the מחלוקת that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'is offered' do not say exactly when the offering counts as done. So the ברייתא does not settle the debate. Each side can read it according to his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: For one Sage, as he holds
And for the other Sage, as he holds

phrases.english: 'Once the handful is offered.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the words of the ברייתא from step 6.

phrases.english: For one Sage, as he holds,
and for the other Sage, as he holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ וּלְמָר כִּדְאִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wording of step 6 to show it fits more than one view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phrase 'once the קומץ is offered' is flexible enough to fit both sides of the מחלוקת.

steps.title: When does the קומץ permit the leftovers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the question at the center of the מחלוקת: from what moment does the קומץ permit the שיריים to be eaten?
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: from when does the handful permit the leftovers to be eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known debate that begins with a question: at what point does burning the קומץ make the leftovers permitted? This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6 and 8 already showed that the קומץ permits the שיריים. The new question is about timing: which stage of the burning counts.

phrases.english: As it was stated: the handful, from when
does it permit the leftovers to be eaten?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: הַקּוֹמֶץ, מֵאֵימָתַי מַתִּיר שִׁירַיִים בַּאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the debate that step 9 referred to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact moment in the burning of the קומץ when the שיריים become permitted.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: when the fire catches; רבי יוחנן: when most is burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the שיריים become permitted once the fire takes hold of the קומץ. רבי יוחנן says only once the fire has burned most of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: from when the fire takes hold of it. רבי יוחנן says: from when the fire has burned most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers about when the leftovers become permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי חנינא, the קומץ counts as offered as soon as it catches fire. For רבי יוחנן, it counts only when most of it has been burned. Each one reads the ברייתא's 'once the קומץ is offered' according to his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: From when the fire takes hold of it
From when the fire has burned most of it

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says:
From when the fire takes hold of it,
Rabbi Yochanan says:
From when the fire has burned most of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: מִשֶּׁתִּשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ הָאוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חנינא: as soon as the fire catches the קומץ. רבי יוחנן: once most of it is burned.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's words 'once the קומץ is offered' fit both views. רבי חנינא says the moment the fire catches; רבי יוחנן says when most of it is burned.
steps.whyThisMatters: The timing decides from what moment the כהנים may eat the rest of the מנחה.

steps.title: The כהנים may season the leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the כהנים may add wine, oil and honey to the leftover מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the כהנים are allowed to put wine, oil and honey into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds a new rule. When the כהנים eat the leftovers, they are allowed to mix in wine, oil and honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps covered when the שיריים may be eaten. Now the ברייתא tells us how they may be eaten: the כהנים may make them tasty. This is a permission, and it does not obligate them to do anything.

phrases.english: And the priests are permitted
to put into it wine, oil and honey.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the leftover part of the מנחה that the כהנים eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues past the מחלוקת about timing and adds a rule about how the שיריים may be eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים may add wine, oil and honey to the leftover מנחה.

steps.title: Why may they add these things?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the כהנים are allowed to add these things. This question sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a holy offering should be eaten plain, with nothing added. So the גמרא wants a source that shows adding flavor is allowed.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that allows the כהנים to season the leftover מנחה.

steps.title: Eaten like kings eat
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the gifts are given 'למשחה,' which means for greatness, so the כהנים eat them the way kings do.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'למשחה,' meaning for greatness, in the way that kings eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The gifts are given to the כהנים 'למשחה,' and that word means 'for greatness.' So they may eat them in a royal way, with fancy additions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word למשחה usually means anointing. Here the גמרא reads it as honor and greatness. Kings eat their food well prepared, so the כהנים may flavor their portion too.

keyTerms.meaning: for anointing; read here as 'for greatness'

phrases.english: The verse states: 'for a consecrated portion,' meaning for greatness,
in the manner that kings eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: למשחה means for greatness, so the כהנים may eat their portion like kings, with seasonings.

steps.title: The one limit: it may not become חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes: the only thing forbidden to the כהנים is letting the leftovers become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they are forbidden only from letting it become leavened.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by giving the one restriction. The כהנים may add whatever they like, but they may not let the leftovers become חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the wide permission in step 12, this step sets the single boundary: the כהנים may add flavorings, but they may not let the leftovers become חמץ. The next step gives the פסוק behind this limit.

phrases.english: And they are prohibited only from allowing it to become leavened,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit on the permission given in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover מנחה may not be made חמץ.

steps.title: Even their portion may not be חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'לא תאפה חמץ חלקם,' which ריש לקיש reads as 'even their portion shall not be baked as חמץ.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'It shall not be baked as חמץ, their portion.' ריש לקיש said: even their portion shall not be baked as חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the חמץ rule. ריש לקיש explains how to read the פסוק so that it teaches this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the words 'their portion' would start a new phrase. ריש לקיש attaches them to 'shall not be baked as חמץ.' So the ban on חמץ covers even the part given to the כהנים, which is the שיריים.

keyTerms.meaning: it shall not be baked as leaven

steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים may eat the leftovers like kings, with wine, oil and honey. The only limit is חמץ.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'It shall not be baked with leaven. Their portion,'
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
Even their portion shall not be baked with leaven.
phrases.notes: He reads 'their portion' as part of the same sentence, so it covers the כהנים' share too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the restriction in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the leftover מנחה may not become חמץ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 6:10, read by ריש לקיש as 'even their portion shall not be baked as חמץ.'

steps.title: But the sinner's מנחה has no oil or frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, 'all מנחות need oil and frankincense,' and challenges it from the מנחת חוטא, which the תורה says has neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All the מנחות' and so on. Do all מנחות really need oil and frankincense? But there is the מנחת חוטא, about which the תורה says, 'He shall not put oil on it, and he shall not put frankincense on it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes it. Then it attacks the משנה's general statement, because one well-known מנחה has no oil and no frankincense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that every מנחה except the סוטה's needs oil and frankincense. The מנחת חוטא is a clear exception written in the תורה. So the משנה's statement looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: the מנחה brought by a poor sinner

phrases.english: The mishna states: All meal-offerings, etc.
But do all meal-offerings require oil and frankincense?
But isn't there the meal-offering of a sinner,
about which the Merciful One states: 'He shall put no oil upon it,'
'neither shall he put any frankincense on it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הַמְּנָחוֹת טְעוּנוֹת שֶׁמֶן וּלְבוֹנָה? וְהָאִיכָּא מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא discussion is finished, and the גמרא returns to the משנה with a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that all מנחות need oil and frankincense.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מנחת חוטא has neither oil nor frankincense, so the general statement cannot be true as written.

steps.title: The סוטה's מנחה is different in both ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה lists two features of regular מנחות. Other unusual מנחות differ in only one of them, while the סוטה's differs in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means. All מנחות need oil and frankincense, are brought from wheat, and are brought as fine flour. The מנחת חוטא has no oil or frankincense, but it is still wheat and fine flour. The מנחת העומר is barley, but it still needs oil and frankincense and is brought as groats. But this one, the סוטה's, has no oil or frankincense, is barley, and is brought as plain flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה never claimed every מנחה has oil and frankincense. Its point is that the סוטה's מנחה is the only one that is different in both ways at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two features: oil and frankincense, and wheat as fine flour. The מנחת חוטא lacks only the first feature, and the עומר lacks only the second. The סוטה's מנחה lacks both, and that is what makes it unique.

keyTerms.meaning: the barley offering brought on the second day of פסח

steps.whatToRemember: The סוטה's מנחה is the only מנחה that has no oil or frankincense and is also barley flour. Other unusual מנחות differ in only one of these.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the עומר and the סוטה's מנחה. Both are barley, but only the סוטה's has no oil or frankincense.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
All meal-offerings require oil and frankincense,
and are brought from wheat, and are brought as fine flour.

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה שֶׁמֶן וּלְבוֹנָה —
phrases.english: The meal-offering of a sinner, even though it does not require oil and frankincense,
is brought from wheat and brought as fine flour.

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִין —
phrases.english: The omer meal-offering, even though it is brought from barley,
requires oil and frankincense and is brought as groats.

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ, אֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה לֹא שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא לְבוֹנָה,
phrases.english: But this one requires neither oil nor frankincense,
and is brought from barley, and is brought as plain flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by rereading the משנה's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that every other מנחה has oil and frankincense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means the סוטה's מנחה is unique because it differs from regular מנחות in both features. The מנחת חוטא and the עומר each differ in only one.

steps.title: A sinner's flour offering should have had oil and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון teaches that logic would require the מנחת חוטא to have oil and frankincense, so a sinner wouldn't save money. The תורה leaves them out so that his offering won't be fancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון said: By right, the sinner's flour offering should need oil and frankincense, so that a sinner should not come out ahead. So why does it not need them? So that his offering should not be beautiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains why the מנחת חוטא, which we just saw has no oil or frankincense, is made that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a logical pull in one direction: leaving out the extras saves the sinner money, which seems like a reward for sinning. But the תורה goes the other way on purpose. A sinner's offering should be plain, not decorated.

keyTerms.meaning: By right / logically it should be
The flour offering of a sinner (a poor person who can't afford an animal)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
By right, the meal-offering of a sinner should
require oil and frankincense,
so that a sinner should not gain.
And for what reason does it not require them?
So that his offering will not be of fine quality.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: בְּדִין הוּא שֶׁתְּהֵא מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the exception mentioned in steps 17-18, that the מנחת חוטא has no oil or frankincense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת חוטא lacks oil and frankincense so that a sinner's offering is not made beautiful, even though this saves him money.

steps.title: The same reasoning for a חטאת brought for eating חלב
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון applies the same logic to a חטאת animal brought for eating forbidden fat. It should have needed נסכים, but it doesn't, so that it won't be fancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by right, a חטאת for eating forbidden fat should need נסכים, so that a sinner should not come out ahead. So why does it not need them? So that his offering should not be beautiful.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון continues his teaching and applies the same idea to an animal חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burnt offerings and peace offerings come with נסכים (flour, oil and wine). A חטאת does not. The reason matches the מנחת חוטא: a sinner's offering is kept plain.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering brought for eating forbidden fat by mistake
Libations: the flour, oil and wine that go along with many animal offerings

phrases.english: And by right, a sin-offering for forbidden fat should
require libations,
so that a sinner should not gain.
And for what reason does it not require them?
So that his offering will not be of fine quality.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִין הוּא שֶׁתְּהֵא חַטַּאת חֵלֶב טְעוּנָה נְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי שמעון's reasoning from the flour offering to an animal חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת for eating חלב has no נסכים so that a sinner's offering is not beautiful.

steps.title: The מצורע's offerings do get נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that the מצורע's חטאת and אשם do need נסכים, because they are not brought for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חטאת and אשם of a מצורע do need נסכים, because they do not come for a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון shows the other side of his rule: offerings not brought for a sin are not kept plain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for leaving out the extras was that the person sinned. A מצורע brings a חטאת and אשם for a different reason, so his offerings get נסכים like normal offerings. This sets up the questions in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with the skin affliction צרעת

phrases.english: But the sin-offering of a leper and his guilt-offering
require libations,
because they do not come on account of a sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל חַטָּאתוֹ שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע וַאֲשָׁמוֹ טְעוּנִין נְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the sinner's offerings with offerings that do not come for a sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings not brought for a sin, like the מצורע's חטאת and אשם, do require נסכים.

steps.title: But צרעת comes because of sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the מצורע's offerings are not for a sin, quoting רבי יונתן that צרעת comes because of seven sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: צרעת comes because of seven things (sins), etc.!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 21. If צרעת is caused by sin, then the מצורע's offerings seem to be connected to sin after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's rule depends on the מצורע not being a sinner. A well-known teaching says צרעת is a punishment for specific sins. So the מצורע's offerings should be kept plain too.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani say
that Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שִׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים נְגָעִים בָּאִין וְכוּ׳!
phrases.english: Leprous afflictions come on account of seven matters, etc.!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the מצורע's offerings are not brought for a sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צרעת is caused by sin, so the offerings that end the צרעת seem to be sin-related and should lack נסכים.

steps.title: The צרעת itself already atoned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the צרעת itself atoned for the sin. The offering comes only to allow him to eat קדשים again.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he already received atonement through his צרעת. When he brings the offering, he brings it only to become permitted to eat holy foods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון: the sin did cause the צרעת, but the offering itself is not for that sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suffering of צרעת already wiped away the sin. By the time he brings his offerings, their job is only to make him fit to eat קדשים. So they are not sin offerings in purpose, and they get נסכים.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule depends on why the offering is brought now, not on whether a sin was ever involved in the story.

phrases.english: There, it is from his affliction that he gained atonement,
when he brings an offering,
it is to become permitted in sacrificial food that he brings it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since צרעת comes from sin, the מצורע's offerings atone for sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The צרעת already atoned; the offerings only permit him to eat קדשים, so they are not for a sin.

steps.title: Then the נזיר's חטאת should get נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if offerings not brought for a sin get נסכים, then the נזיר's חטאת should get them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the חטאת of a נזיר should need נסכים, since it does not come for a sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבי שמעון's rule on another case, the חטאת a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the rule of step 21, any offering not brought for a sin should get נסכים. A נזיר seems to have done nothing wrong. The question assumes his חטאת does not get נסכים, so the rule seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so (introduces a challenge from the previous logic)
The sin-offering a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות

phrases.english: But if that is so,
the sin-offering of a nazirite should require libations,
because it does not come on account of a sin!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, חַטַּאת נָזִיר תְּהֵא טְעוּנָה נְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of steps 21-23 to a new case and finds a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule that offerings not for a sin require נסכים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נזיר's חטאת is not for a sin, yet it lacks נסכים, which contradicts the rule.

steps.title: A נזיר is also considered a sinner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון holds like רבי אלעזר הקפר, who says a נזיר is also a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds like רבי אלעזר הקפר, who said: a נזיר is also a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון by showing that, in his view, the נזיר's חטאת really is connected to a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר הקפר, a נזיר did something wrong by denying himself wine without need. So his חטאת is a sinner's offering and stays plain, without נסכים. The rule from step 21 holds.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's rule: a sinner's offering is kept plain (no oil, frankincense or נסכים). Offerings not for a sin, like the מצורע's, get נסכים. The נזיר counts as a sinner.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Elazar HaKappar,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי שמעון, the author of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: who said: A nazirite is also a sinner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes a position to the speaker (רבי שמעון follows another תנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נזיר did nothing wrong, so his חטאת is not for a sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי אלעזר הקפר, a נזיר is a sinner, so his חטאת is a sinner's offering and has no נסכים.

steps.title: Quoting רבן גמליאל's teaching from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the opening words of רבן גמליאל's statement about the סוטה's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבן גמליאל says, "Just as..." and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the opening words of רבן גמליאל's line in the משנה. This prepares the next step, where a ברייתא adds more about his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן גמליאל said that just as the סוטה acted like an animal, her offering (the מנחת סוטה) is made of barley, which is animal food. The גמרא only quotes the first words and writes "כו׳" to point to the rest of the line.

keyTerms.meaning: "Etc." It tells you the quote goes on, so finish the line from the משנה
The meal offering a סוטה brings, which is made of barley

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
"Just as," etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is: just as her actions were like an animal's, her offering is animal food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of נסכים for the מצורע and נזיר and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה's offering is animal food (barley) because her actions were like an animal's.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל asks to explain the teaching as a symbolic lesson
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבן גמליאל asked the חכמים for permission to explain the barley offering as a חומר, a decorative and symbolic kind of explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבן גמליאל said to the חכמים, "Scribes, let me explain it as a kind of חומר (a decorative wreath, meaning a symbolic lesson)."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבן גמליאל asks permission to give a symbolic explanation of the barley offering. This line sets up the actual explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already gave the basic idea: animal-like actions lead to animal food. In this ברייתא, רבן גמליאל says he wants to go further and teach it as a חומר, a symbolic explanation that decorates the law like a wreath. He politely asks the חכמים first, calling them "סופרים".

keyTerms.meaning: Scribes, a respectful way of addressing the חכמים
I will explain it (give a דרשה on it)
A decorative wreath, meaning a symbolic or allegorical explanation

steps.confusionAlert: Here חוֹמֶר does not mean "קל וחומר" or "stringency." It means a decorative, symbolic kind of explanation.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabban Gamliel said to the Sages:
Scribes, allow me,
and I will explain it as a kind of decorative wreath.
phrases.notes: He means a symbolic lesson that decorates the law, the way a wreath decorates something.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on רבן גמליאל's statement in the משנה and gets ready to give his symbolic explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל plans to explain the barley offering as a symbolic lesson (חומר).
